newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - WMC says to pursue growth strategy.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - WMC says to pursue growth strategy.

text.p: Gold and nickel miner WMC Ltd said on Thursday it would continue to pursue its growth strategy and lower costs while optimising asset value.
The stronger exchange rate reduced the improvement in sales revenue, WMC said.
Nickel profit for the year rose 26.4 percent to A$314.9 million, due to higher production, higher sales volumes and a higher nickel price.

The contribution to equity profit from WMC's 40 percent interest in Alcoa World Alumina (AWA), an alumina joint venture with Aluminum Co of America, rose to A$299.6 million from A$231.4 million in 1995.
Gold profit fell to A$63.6 million, due to lower production and higher costs.
Profit from the copper-uranium business rose to A$123.1 million from A$102 million due to record copper production and sales from Olympic Dam.
Petroleum profits fell to A$14.2 million from A$14.9 million.
WMC's shares closed eight cents lower at A$8.59, but had been A$8.61 just before the results were released.
"WMC will continue to pursue its growth strategy," WMC Managing Director Hugh Morgan said in a statement.
"Our objective is to maximise shareholder value by finding, acquiring, developing and operating mineral resource projects throughout the world," Morgan said.
"At existing operations WMC will pursue lower costs while optimising asset value," he said.
Earlier WMC reported a 20.4 percent rise in net equity profit to A$386.2 million for the year to June 30, 1996 and posted an 11 cent final dividend, up from 12 cents.
